sources.title: Aesthetics Wiki — Vectordelia

name: Vectorgarden
description: Botanical vector flourishes, butterflies, translucent curls, and luminous gradients create a delicate digital garden.
distinction: A nature-focused branch of vector ornament, distinguished from Vectordelia's music, urban silhouettes, and denser graphic bursts.

sources.title: Aesthetics Wiki — Vectorgarden

description: Clean white surfaces, gentle curves, small friendly symbols, and restrained natural accents suggest calm everyday technology.
distinction: A retrospective look associated with 2000s Japanese consumer technology; quieter and less scenic than Frutiger Aero.

sources.title: Aesthetics Wiki — Technozen

distinction: Its craft ethic and ornamental page construction differ from Art Nouveau's flowing modern line.

sources.title: V&A — Arts and Crafts: an introduction

name: Synthwave

sources.title: Original Obsidian handbook — Synthwave

name: Cyberpunk

distinction: Combines advanced technology with social friction and decay, rather than treating luminous technology as automatically optimistic.

sources.title: Linearity — Cyberpunk: how to master the futuristic style

sources.title: RGD — Hyperpop and Acidgrafix

name: Global Village Coffeehouse

distinction: Uses irregular symbolic illustration and historically borrowed cultural motifs, rather than Frasurbane's polished classical imagery.

sources.title: CARI — Global Village Coffeehouse

name: Corporate Grunge
description: Distressed type, rough textures, tilted fragments, and compressed layouts bring 1990s alternative graphics into advertising.

sources.title: CARI — Corporate Grunge

sources.title: CARI — Corporate Hippie

sources.title: CARI — Utopian Scholastic

sources.title: CARI — Factory Pomo

description: Celestial emblems, curling shapes, dark jewel tones, and eccentric ornament make gothic imagery playful and dreamlike.
distinction: Combines whimsy with gothic theatricality; unlike ordinary goth styling, its forms often feel storybook-like.

sources.title: CARI — Whimsigothic

name: Whimsicraft
description: Colorful folk shapes, found-object collage, visible joins, and handmade textures celebrate playful assembly.
distinction: The craft revival's assembled material character differs from flat whimsical illustration.

sources.title: CARI — Whimsicraft

description: Loose hand lettering, offbeat drawings, mundane objects, and knowingly awkward retro cues create a twee indie vernacular.
distinction: Associated with 2000s indie consumer culture; its deadpan everyday humor differs from expansive craft ornament.

sources.title: CARI — Hipness Purgatory

distinction: A vernacular of low-budget production and improvised software use, rather than a single intentional design movement.

sources.title: CARI — Dollar Store Vernacular

distinction: The object-led reduction of Sachplakat differs from Swiss Style's extended information grids.

sources.title: National Museum of Modern Art, Kyoto — Modern German Posters

description: Oversized geometric stripes, rounded futuristic forms, rainbow bands, and confident sans-serif type create a playful synthetic future.
distinction: Its 1960s–1970s supergraphic scale and plastic-age optimism precede Y2K's digital chrome.

sources.title: CARI — Supergraphic Ultramodern

name: Steampunk
description: Engraved ornament, brass-like surfaces, mechanical diagrams, and Victorian lettering imagine an alternate industrial technology.
distinction: A speculative historical aesthetic, distinct from actual Victorian graphic artifacts or generic metallic rendering.

sources.title: Original Obsidian handbook — Steampunk

name: Afrofuturism
description: Cosmic imagery, speculative technology, and references to African diaspora histories envision liberated Black futures.
distinction: A cultural and artistic framework centered on Black agency, not a single palette or interchangeable futuristic motif.

sources.title: Smithsonian NMAAHC — Afrofuturism

name: Impressionism
description: Broken touches of color and soft shifting edges capture momentary light and everyday atmosphere.
distinction: Observed light and fleeting perception distinguish it from the non-naturalistic color of Fauvism.

sources.title: Tate — Impressionism

name: Post-Internet Aesthetic
description: Digital gradients, altered documentation, borrowed online imagery, and physical media artifacts circulate between screen and object.
distinction: Concerns art made within pervasive network culture; unlike Net Art, the work need not exist only online.

sources.title: Artie Vierkant — Image Objects

name: New Aesthetic
description: Machine vision, mapping artifacts, pixels, and computational patterns reveal digital perception inside ordinary physical life.
distinction: James Bridle's research project concerns how machines see the world, rather than any generic futuristic appearance.

sources.title: James Bridle — The New Aesthetic

name: Art Brut
description: Personal symbols, unconventional figures, dense marks, and idiosyncratic construction emerge outside academic artistic conventions.
distinction: A category associated with independent, self-taught creation; roughness alone does not make a work Art Brut.

sources.title: Tate — Art brut

name: Surrealism
description: Dream logic, impossible combinations, transformed objects, and unexpected scale challenge ordinary perception.
distinction: A historical movement exploring the unconscious, distinct from Pop Surrealism's later cartoon and popular-culture vocabulary.

sources.title: Tate — Surrealism

name: Cubism
description: Fragmented planes and overlapping viewpoints reconstruct objects as a compact field of shapes.
distinction: Simultaneous viewpoints distinguish Cubist construction from decorative geometric abstraction.

sources.title: Tate — Cubism

name: Fauvism
description: Intense non-naturalistic color, simplified forms, and assertive brushwork make color the main organizing force.
distinction: The expressive use of arbitrary color differs from Impressionism's effort to observe changing natural light.

sources.title: Tate — Fauvism

name: Photomontage
description: Cut, combined, and rescaled photographs construct a new scene, argument, or impossible relationship.
distinction: Photographic source fragments are essential; this differs from collage built mainly from paper, lettering, or found objects.

sources.title: Tate — Photomontage
